Product documentation says the public endpoint requires no sign-in or API key. However, prefetched protected-resource metadata for this exact endpoint returns HTTP 200 and advertises authorization server https://developer.api.autodesk.com/mcpauth, scopes mcp:read, mcp:write, offline_access, and bearer header support. The authorization-server metadata advertises authorization_code, client_credentials, refresh_token; PKCE S256; client auth none, client_secret_basic, client_secret_post; client_id_metadata_document_supported true; no registration_endpoint is listed. Token lifetime is not provided. Metadata reports a revocation endpoint.

D_server_side_logic.additional_logic: 1. Tools are read-only per Autodesk; no write or destructive operations are listed. Official tool reference does not publish annotation fields such as readOnlyHint or destructiveHint. 2. No server-enforced confirmation flow is described; operations only retrieve public documentation. 3. Docs say no sign-in is required and no Autodesk-side allowlisting is needed. Protected-resource metadata nevertheless advertises mcp:read, mcp:write, offline_access and an OAuth authorization server. Product-user permission inheritance, token lifetime, and client allowlisting are not documented. 4. A single public endpoint is documented. No read-only URL mode, tool filter, sandbox, or regional variant for this endpoint was found. 5. Autodesk says the plugin accesses public-facing information and does not access model or user data; no query masking or personal-data filtering is described. 6. No call quotas, rate limits, result caps beyond the optional max_results default of 5, or usage costs per call are documented. 7. Required fields and input validation are documented; query has minimum length 2. Product and release filters should use exact values from the product catalog; docs advise omitting uncertain filters. Unknown-argument handling and coercion are not described. 8. Server logging, audit trails, and telemetry behavior are not documented. 9. Tool list contains no feedback/rating/survey or vendor-reporting tool; no upsell response mechanism documented. 10. No server-delivered skill tool. Docs contain recommendations to clients and users; enforcement by server is not established. 11. No persistent agent memory or stateful personalization is documented. 12. Flat documented tool list; the docs note tool availability can vary by endpoint/audience, but do not enumerate variants for this endpoint. 13. No raw API, SQL, script, or arbitrary request tool is listed.
behavioural_instructions_to_ai_verbatim: Treat product values as a closed set: use exact values returned by get_available_products (don’t normalize or change casing).
locale: Locale used to scope search/results (language/region). Use the locale from the user’s context (do not guess).
If you can’t confidently map a request to an allowed value (product/release/locale), omit the field and retry. For required locale, use the locale from context (do not guess).
Don’t include sensitive data in queries (credentials, secrets, personal data).

E_aggregated.human_can_agent_cannot: People can browse Autodesk Help directly and navigate pages, but the documented MCP tool set exposes only product/release discovery and content search. Autodesk describes the server as read-only; it cannot write to Autodesk, software, or user accounts. The server does not expose Autodesk product operations or model/user data through this endpoint.

F_documentation.implementation_hints_not_enforced: Documentation recommends exact product/release values from get_available_products, context-derived locales, keyword-rich queries, and avoiding sensitive query data. These are client/agent recommendations; public server-side enforcement is not fully documented. Verbatim guidance is recorded in D.
F_documentation.governance_promises: Autodesk says the service is read-only, covers public-facing help content, and does not access model or user data; the ChatGPT plugin cannot write data back to Autodesk, software, or accounts.
F_documentation.promises_to_user: Autodesk describes the content as official, trusted, up to date, and available across 110+ products. Server availability is stated to be at no cost.
F_documentation.comparison_with_server_logic: The two documented tools are retrieval-only, consistent with read-only claims. Public docs establish tool names and input validation but do not expose server code or enough response details to independently verify data handling, retention, logging, or every security claim.

contradictions: Product Help setup documentation says the public endpoint requires no authentication, while exact-path OAuth protected-resource metadata returns HTTP 200 and advertises scopes mcp:read, mcp:write, offline_access and an Autodesk authorization server. The endpoint itself returned HTTP 400 for the prefetched POST probe with “Invalid Content-Type header”; this does not establish whether OAuth is required for normal requests.
OAuth metadata advertises mcp:write for an endpoint Autodesk describes as read-only and whose official tool reference lists only read operations.
observations_for_research: Tool guidance asks agents to treat product and release values as a closed set supplied by a discovery tool and to use a context-derived locale.
The documentation emphasizes runtime tool discovery and says tool availability can vary by endpoint or audience, although it provides two tools for the supplied public endpoint.
